'''''Choisya ternata''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Rutaceae]],<ref name=TPL_kew-2719292/> known as '''Mexican orange blossom''' or '''Mexican orange'''.

==Description==
''Choisya ternata'' is an evergreen shrub, growing up to {{cvt|3|m|0}} in height. Its leaves have three leaflets (hence ''ternata'') and are aromatic, releasing a smell reminiscent of [[basil]] when crushed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mexican mock orange - KPU Plant DB |url=https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/Plant/chte |website=plantdatabase.kpu.ca |access-date=12 March 2024}}</ref> The white flowers are scented, appearing in spring (sometimes with limited repeat flowering in autumn).<ref name=PhilRix89/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Choisya ternata'' originates from [[Mexico]]. It is drought tolerant, preferring well drained soils.<ref name=PhilRix89/>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Choisya 'Aztec Pearl' detail.JPG|thumb|175px|''Choisya'' 'Aztec Pearl']]
''Choisya ternata'' is widely grown as an ornamental shrub in suitable climates. It tolerates temperatures down to {{cvt|-10|C}} but is severely damaged by temperatures lower than {{cvt|-15|C}}. It responds well to pruning and shaping.<ref name=PhilRix89/>

In addition to the species, a number of [[cultivar]]s are grown, including the golden-leaved ''C. ternata'' 'Lich' (usually sold under the name {{tdes|Sundance}}),<ref name=RHS_PS426/> and the [[Hybrid (biology)#Interspecific hybrids|inter-specific hybrid]] ''C.'' 'Aztec Pearl' (''[[Choisya dumosa|C. dumosa]]'' var. ''arizonica'' × ''C. ternata'').<ref name=RHS_PS425/> The species and these two cultivars have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].

==Phytochemistry==
Many [[quinoline alkaloids]] have been isolated from leaves of ''C. ternata''.<ref name=Boyd07/> ''C. ternata'' contains an alkaloid (ternanthranin), a volatile simple [[anthranilate]], that was shown to have [[pain-killing]] effects in mice.<ref name=RaduMiltMcDeWald11/>
